references.text: The immediate context describes how the earth opened up and swallowed Korah, Dathan, and Abiram along with their families and possessions, explaining why the people fled in fear.
Lot was told to flee for his life when Sodom and Gomorrah were about to be destroyed, a similar example of fleeing from God's judgment.
The Egyptians fled when they realized that the Lord was fighting for Israel, an example of flight driven by fear of God's intervention.
Moses reminds the people how the earth opened up and swallowed Dathan and Abiram, a direct reference to the same event.
The psalm describes how the earth opened up and swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram's company, a poetic retelling of the event.
Isaiah describes how Sheol opens its mouth, an image resembling the earth opening up to swallow people.
